Abstract:In computer vision, vision-language and self-supervised encoders are two unique paradigms characterized by global language alignment and high-quality vision-only patch representations, respectively. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often use the former because of language alignment, despite the recent rise in vision-centric tasks resembling traditional dense vision tasks that would likely benefit from the high-quality patch representations, raising the question whether self-supervised models could aid MLLMs in vision-centric tasks. To investigate this, we define semantic (in)consistency of patch tokens from language-aligned encoders and identify two sets of tokens, semantically consistent (SCTs) and semantically inconsistent (SITs). Through systematic probing via the removal of SCTs or SITs from the input of modern MLLMs, we show higher reliance on SCTs than SITs, as removal of the former induces larger performance drops. This demonstrates that MLLMs benefit from semantic consistency of vision tokens. With this in mind, we devise a simple yet effective extension of the MLLM training objective that combines traditional language modeling with semantic guidance via minimization of semantic inconsistency. This strategy, named Semantically-Guided Training (SGT), combines the signals of both loss terms to push the vision encoder towards providing semantically consistent tokens, while preserving language alignment. Extensive evaluation shows that SGT outperforms all baselines and MLLMs with specialized vision encoders on vision-centric benchmarks while keeping strong scores on text-centric benchmarks, thus setting state of the art on average across all tasks. Our results highlight the importance of combining language alignment and semantic consistency through the lens of MLLMs rather than independently from them and pave the way towards the design of better MLLM vision encoders.

Abstract:We propose SteinPnP, a probabilistic Perspective- N-Point (PnP) solver that models the full 6-DoF camera pose posterior using a non-parametric set of pose particles. However, a naive application of SVI struggles in the PnP problem, often missing alternative pose hypotheses or assigning incorrect probability weights to them. To address these limitations, we propose practical remedies that discover new potential poses, identify distinct hypothesis clusters, and balance their relative probability weights to capture the true underlying distribution. Our experiments across synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that SteinPnP accurately captures complex multimodal uncertainties while maintaining competitive accuracy.

Abstract:Thermal infrared imaging is vital for applications like search-and-rescue and autonomous navigation, yet trans- lating it into 3D scene representations remains a critical bottleneck. Fur- thermore, existing thermal reconstruction methods rely heavily on dense capture and computationally expensive per-scene optimization. Trained on an aggregated multi-source dataset, ThermalSplat synthesizes sharp reconstructions of unseen scenes in a single feed-forward pass. Extensive experi- ments demonstrate that ThermalSplat holds a strict advan- tage over scene-specific thermal splatting methods in the sparse regime. Furthermore, even compared against these baselines operating under their ideal dense capture set- tings, ThermalSplat achieves superior perceptual fidelity. By eliminating the need for computationally expensive per scene optimization, ThermalSplat offers an efficient and generalizable approach to thermal 3D reconstruction.

Abstract:Automatic evaluation is now central to text-to-image benchmarking, but the verifier that converts generated images into scores is often treated as an implementation detail. On a balanced 2,280-image evaluation split, aggregate score matching can coexist with image-level disagreement, and verifier-use protocols and generator distributions change the measured reliability. Every verifier-protocol configuration also shrinks the human score difference between the two generators, by 7.5-25.0 pp, and with a third generator, Z-Image, all four tested protocols reverse the human ordering of Z-Image and FLUX.2-dev on our fixed prompt suite. Abstract:Scene graphs provide a compact, structured representation of environments by capturing objects and their spatial or semantic relationships in a form suitable for embodied agents. Our method leverages a Parametric Relation Predictor (PRP) that learns to estimate pairwise distances and relative angles between objects from 2D visual features and 2D geometric cues, using 3D geometric supervision available only during training. These learned pairwise measurements are fused across views through Pose Graph Optimization (PGO)~\cite{grisetti2010tutorial} to recover metrically grounded 3D object positions and build a globally consistent 3D scene graph incrementally. 131. 【2611.15420】Learning Motion-Appearance Coupling Priors for Solving Video Inverse Problems

Abstract:Reconstructing video from degraded measurements requires priors that capture both frame appearance and temporal dynamics. Many recent approaches combine pretrained image diffusion priors with motion guidance, sidestepping the costs of training large video models. Temporal consistency is often enforced via photometric losses or warping-based constraints, which implicitly assume that motion explains frame-to-frame or latent-to-latent changes up to small deviations, an assumption that fails under occlusions, lighting changes, and non-rigid deformation. In this paper, we propose to learn the coupling between motion and frame appearance as a generative prior. We learn the distribution of motion-induced appearance residuals with a conditional diffusion model and use it to regularize reconstruction in video inverse problems. Our motion-appearance prior acts as a plug-in regularizer for diffusion-based video reconstruction, preserving the benefits of image diffusion models while remaining compatible with existing appearance regularization techniques. Experiments on dynamic video inverse problems show that reconstruction with a learnt motion-appearance coupling prior outperforms photometric-consistency and noise-warping baselines, and that the approach also transfers to cardiac MRI reconstruction.

Abstract:Infographic charts communicate data through cohesive compositions of visual elements such as charts, text, and images. To address this limitation, we introduce ChartGalaxy++, a richly annotated dataset of 217,195 infographic charts. At the core of this dataset is a scene graph representation, in which nodes represent visual elements and semantic groups, and edges encode their hierarchical and spatial relationships. Abstract:Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refinement into waypoint residual correction and position-conditioned heading generation. Through imitation learning and a future-token auxiliary task, the backbone provides predictive representations and a base trajectory. The position expert predicts bounded metric waypoint residuals, while the heading expert reconstructs vehicle orientation from adjacent angular increments conditioned on the corrected path. With the backbone frozen, the two experts are optimized alternately through supervised initialization and reinforcement fine-tuning. Abstract:Merging datasets labelled at different levels of a taxonomy leaves some images with only a coarse label, and some classes with no fine-grained label at all. Standard training scores a coarse label by the total probability of the classes under it. Coarse labels name superclasses, and the standard objective is exact only when every class within a superclass is equally likely to receive a coarse label. We call a class novel if it is never labelled finely, and known otherwise. A novel class violates the assumption, and the classifier assigns its images to a known sibling. We propose Arbor, which models how labels become coarse. In each superclass with a novel class, Arbor adds a virtual novel class, and a logistic gate divides the superclass's probability between it and the known classes. The gate is trained with the likelihood of the observed labels under this model, the coarsening likelihood. We prove that at its population optimum the gate equals the Elkan-Noto correction of positive-unlabelled learning, and show that training the correction into the classifier improves on applying it after training. Across Cars, CUB and Aircraft with 90% coarse labels, Arbor correctly assigns 76-85% of novel-class images to their superclass, more than hierarchical classifiers, hierarchical novelty detection and the Elkan-Noto correction. Its top-1 accuracy over the leaf classes on known-class images is within 1.6 points of the best baseline, although its final predictions return the superclass more often. On the more challenging iNaturalist-2019 benchmark, Arbor improves novel-class accuracy from 46% (uniform target, the strongest baseline) to 68%.

Abstract:Plan-conditioned driving world models are used to compare candidate plans, so their forecast should change with the plan as the real scene would, yet widely used control metrics check only whether the camera follows the command. ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers. Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

Abstract:\textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. We trace this to a recall bottleneck rather than a mask-quality one, and address it with a training-free, modular system. The pipeline first generates high-recall object proposals using an off-the-shelf class-agnostic detector, then matches each proposal to the reference using foundation-model features (e.g., BLIP-2), and finally refines the selected box with SAM. For robust matching we propose \textbf{top-$K$ Sinkhorn}, a patch-level distance that scores each candidate only on its most confidently matched patches; trimming the Sinkhorn dual potentials recovers the robustness of partial optimal transport at more than $100\times$ lower cost, keeping it inside the per-proposal candidate loop. To evaluate this regime, we introduce \textbf{\datasetname}, a realistic multi-instance benchmark. Across \datasetname, PerSeg, PerMIS, and DAVIS, our system surpasses PerSAM, $\mathrm{P}^2\mathrm{SAM}$, and PDM by up to $\sim\!48$ mIoU while matching their runtime and using fewer parameters, establishing a strong, deployable training-free baseline for real-world personalized segmentation.

Abstract:Vision-Language Models are designed to capture the compositional structure of the world through multi-modal alignment; however, it remains unclear whether their representations truly align with the way a human would naturally describe the same visual input. We introduce GRACE, a method that learns this concept-based structure at the feature space level, producing semantic and general concept decompositions. Abstract:Cross-domain few-shot segmentation (CD-FSS) aims to segment a target class in images from a previously unseen domain using only a few annotated support examples. Although several layer-selection criteria have been proposed, they do not explicitly evaluate whether the predicted query foreground and background labels agree with the corresponding support labels. To address this limitation, we propose a novel layer-selection criterion, Optimal-Transport-Based Backbone Layer Selection (OT-BLS). Our key insight is that an effective layer-selection criterion can be derived from the optimal-transport correspondence between query and support patch-token features. Based on this insight, we first estimate the transport plan using a well-established optimal transport algorithm and then compute a layer-selection score by aggregating the transported mass according to the foreground--background partition defined by each candidate query mask. Abstract:Existing activation steering methods for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) use the global activation mean as the steering vector, which tends to cause cross-task interference and unstable performance. We trace this failure to the multi-centered geometry of task activations. The global mean lands in the empty region between clusters and is faithful to no single task. Moreover, the steering signal in each task-pure local cluster is low-rank, and different query tasks benefit from emphasizing different families of local-basis directions under the shared routing protocol. To address this, we propose MAST (Medoid-Anchored Subspace Steering), a training-free, input-adaptive activation steering framework. MAST groups samples by task, performs multi-center clustering within each group, and selects one representative medoid per cluster. At inference time, each query is routed to multiple representative medoids. For each matched cluster, a low-rank local steering direction is extracted and aggregated across clusters to produce the final steering vector. Building on MAST, MAST-PR (Probe-Reweighted) uses a lightweight task-aware probe to reweight task-specialized local-direction families, yielding a further average improvement of +8.09 points over MAST.

Abstract:Federated learning combines complementary knowledge across clients to alleviate local data limitations without sharing raw samples. However, data heterogeneity can cause conflicting updates and hinder generalization. Update coordination reduces interference among client updates, while flatness optimization reduces sensitivity to parameter perturbations to improve generalization. Existing joint designs largely target specific algorithms, limiting flexible combinations of these approaches. To address this problem, we propose a unified federated learning framework that bridges update coordination and flatness optimization. Clients separately accumulate descent signals and flatness corrections along the same local trajectory. The server coordinates both groups with independent states before fusing their outputs into a global update. Explicit conversion between trajectory signals and model updates enables different coordination strategies to work with compatible local or globally guided flatness mechanisms without changing the inference architecture. Experiments show that the evaluated combinations generally improve average and worst-client accuracy over update coordination alone, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework in combining these complementary optimization mechanisms.

Abstract:3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a mainstream representation for real-time novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction. However, existing 3DGS rendering pipelines are poorly aligned with modern GPU architectures: depth-sorted alpha compositing introduces strong per-pixel sequential dependencies, limiting parallelism and resulting in scalar FMA-dominated execution that underutilizes high-throughput matrix units such as Tensor Cores. This mismatch becomes more severe for multimodal and semantically enriched 3DGS, where high-dimensional features must be accumulated from millions of Gaussians, leading to rapidly increasing computation and memory costs. We propose MatrixSplat, a matrix-parallel rendering framework for feature-scalable 3DGS on modern GPUs. We first identify the sequential dependency of alpha compositing as a key obstacle to efficient high-dimensional feature rendering, and adopt an order-independent weighted accumulation formulation that transforms feature rendering into matrix-oriented computation. Our framework features three key designs: (i) a tile-based splatting pipeline that maps feature accumulation to warp-level matrix-multiply-accumulate execution on Tensor Cores; (ii) a warp-granularity Gaussian packing strategy that mitigates visibility irregularity and improves feature reuse; and (iii) a lazy channel-batched feature-fetching pipeline that reduces shared-memory pressure, maintains high warp occupancy, and overlaps memory access with matrix execution for high-dimensional features. On Mip-NeRF 360, LERF, and 3D-OVS, MatrixSplat achieves up to 3.8$\times$ speedup over 3DGS and 2$\times$ over TC-GS while maintaining rendering quality and semantic accuracy, and further reduces render-kernel time by up to 36.7$\times$ for high-dimensional features. Integrated into existing fast renderers, it provides an additional 1.69-2.84$\times$ speedup.

Abstract:Recent advances in flow-matching Transformers have greatly improved Text-to-Image (T2I) and Text-to-Video (T2V) generation, but unconstrained generation risks producing illegal or unethical content. Safety alignment must therefore suppress unsafe content while preserving legitimate generation. A concept's safety depends on context: a knife used for cooking is safe, whereas its use in violence is harmful. Yet most concept erasure methods indiscriminately suppress static, isolated representations, overlooking evolving semantic interactions. Consequently, safe scenes containing potentially sensitive terms may be unintentionally suppressed, compromising generation quality. To address this, we propose Dynamic Graph Semantic Recomposition (DGSR), which dynamically constructs and updates a semantic interaction graph from evolving text visual states during sampling. Context aware graph reasoning captures semantic dependencies, while paired safe/unsafe supervision distinguishes harmful from legitimate interactions, enabling precise identification of and selective intervention on high risk semantic relationships while preserving benign semantics. DGSR freezes the pretrained backbone and supports both image and video generation. Experiments show that DGSR achieves the lowest Attack Success Rate (ASR) in 10 of 12 T2I evaluations and reduces the average T2V unsafe frame rate by 41.2\% relative to the strongest baseline, while maintaining high generation fidelity and temporal consistency.

Abstract:High-dynamic-range (HDR) displays are now common, but most video content, such as archival footage, broadcast material, and the output of generative video models, exists only in standard dynamic range (SDR). The need is sharpest for generated video, which has no HDR master at all and is graded alongside live-action and visual-effects material finished in HDR. Converting SDR to HDR means undoing a tone-mapping operation that was never recorded, and clipping destroys the radiance wherever it acts, so HDR recovery is a blind inverse problem. Methods built on generative video priors fill clipped regions with plausible structure, but their reconstructions are systematically biased: in every public method we test, saturated content leans too bright or too dark, and the direction of the lean moves with the tone operator behind the input. We call this failure the luminance error, measure both its magnitude and its sign, and make it the focus of this work. Reframing ITM as posterior inference under an unknown operator locates the failure in two places and yields two corrections. A fixed affine functional of the video-diffusion latent reads log-luminance without decoding; on that coordinate an asymmetric loss selects an expectile of the posterior, applied only where clipping leaves luminance unconstrained. We also synthesize training SDR through an explicit family of tone operators, so the model marginalizes over what the observation cannot show. Trained this way, our luminance error stays flatter across operators and smaller on average than any public method, and the full system achieves the best perceptual quality on all three benchmarks.

Abstract:In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

Abstract:Expert review of surgical videos is essential for surgical training but labor-intensive, motivating AI-assisted skill assessment to provide feedback at scale. Although surgical assessment rubrics may use different language to describe similar skills, existing automated methods commonly predict predefined skill levels or numerical scores tied to fixed rubrics, limiting their ability to transfer across semantically equivalent assessment criteria. We propose Predictive Rubric Alignment (PRA), a joint embedding prediction approach that scores surgical videos using natural-language descriptions of skill levels. Rather than matching level probabilities, PRA predicts a rater-weighted combination of skill-level description embeddings. Adjacent description features define a score-parameterized path, and the predicted embedding is projected onto this path to read the score. We introduce two variants: \textit{PRA-item}, which uses learned queries for predefined assessment items, and \textit{PRA-cond}, which generates queries from textual item names to enable assessment of unseen items without retraining. On AIxSuture, a dataset of expert-rated suturing videos, PRA outperforms published baselines in skill classification. We further evaluate zero-shot transfer to the smaller surgical skill assessment benchmark JIGSAWS. Trained on only two AIxSuture rubric items, PRA-cond assesses unseen JIGSAWS items without further training, yielding positive score correlations and greater Grad-CAM overlap with instruments and suture than a description-matching baseline. These results support predictive rubric alignment as a promising direction for flexible and explainable automated surgical skill assessment.

157. 【2611.15107】From Seeing to Remembering: Brain-Informed Agentic Text-to-Video Generation for Enhancing Memorability

Abstract:Generating videos that faithfully convey intended semantics while remaining memorable to viewers is valuable for applications such as advertising, education, and storytelling. In this paper, we propose MemCrafter, brain-informed approach that enhances video memorability through iteratively agentic prompt refinement. The agentic framework contains two key components. First, we construct a cortical region-based neuro-memorability signal that predicts video memorability from estimated neural responses, providing both an optimization objective and interpretable region-level information. Second, we develop a sensitivity-aware feedback module, motivated by a conceptual sensitivity analysis of the optimization objective, to derive actionable guidance for prompt refinement while preserving semantic fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MemCrafter consistently improves predicted video memorability while maintaining semantic alignment and perceptual quality.

Abstract:Long-context multimodal intelligence requires revisiting earlier images as conversations and documents accumulate, yet retaining an image does not guarantee reliable access to its details. We develop static and continuous compensation schedules, using the static schedule by default. Across ten checkpoints and ten benchmarks, static VPR improves 97 of 100 model--task scores. These findings demonstrate an efficient way to sustain visual access through positional adjustment within the cache.

Abstract:Pretrained video world models are compared and chosen as components for robot learning largely by future-prediction scores. On its own, such a score cannot be read as evidence of prediction, because it mixes encoder quality, the near future's resemblance to the recent past, and the predictor's own contribution. We separate the three with a matched control. On 27,000 future-retrieval trials from household egocentric video, a model must pick the true continuation of a clip among eleven candidates from the same video (chance 0.091), ranked zero-shot by its own training criterion. Each model is paired with a persistence control, an identical copy whose predictor is never invoked, so the paired difference isolates the predictor. Score and contribution dissociate within the native-video V-JEPA family alone: the predictor adds +0.291 top-1 for V-JEPA 2.1 but +0.03 to +0.04 for V-JEPA 2 on the identical trials. Across five models the contribution ranges from +0.291 to negative, and it is negative only for the two action-conditioned models, which we evaluate outside their training regime. Persistence alone recovers the encoder ordering expected from pretraining, a sign that the probe tracks real signal. We suggest reporting each future-prediction score together with its persistence baseline. The gap between them, not the score, is what makes the number interpretable: a necessary check costing one forward pass. Establishing downstream usefulness is a separate matter, for a planning or control evaluation.

160. 【2611.15079】SAVE: Less is More in Agentic Video Reasoning

Abstract:Agentic video-reasoning frameworks iteratively explore a video, choosing what to observe based on the query and evidence gathered so far. Existing methods are typically evaluated with different backbones, preprocessing pipelines, and computational budgets, making it difficult to determine which components actually drive performance, how much they cost, and whether agentic inference is preferable to native video reasoning in the first place. We conduct a controlled evaluation of a diverse set of recent agentic video-reasoning systems across two strong contemporary backbones, with explicit token and monetary-cost accounting. Across Gemini 3 Flash and Gemma 4, most existing agentic frameworks fail to consistently improve over native video inference and often increase computational cost. We investigate two primary questions: (1) How much agentic framework complexity is necessary for effective video reasoning? (2) When, if at all, is agentic video reasoning preferable to just using the backbone directly? To answer the first question, we introduce a deliberately minimal Active Exploration Baseline and show that it remains competitive with substantially more elaborate agents. We then propose targeted extensions to this baseline, yielding SAVE (Simple Agentic Video Explorer). SAVE outperforms all evaluated prior agentic methods in five of six backbone-benchmark settings. Turning to the second question, our results indicate that the advantage of agentic exploration grows when dense processing would otherwise represent answer-relevant events too sparsely, particularly for long videos and temporally concentrated evidence. Overall, our results suggest that agentic video reasoning should favor simple frameworks over increasingly elaborate pipelines and focus primarily on long-form video, where selective evidence acquisition offers the clearest advantage over native inference.

Abstract:Visual token pruning reduces the inference cost of multimodal large language models, but answer accuracy only partly reflects its effect. Abstract:Cross-modal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object tracking faces modality-induced appearance discrepancies and abrupt target-position shifts that can arise from modality switching, UAV motion, and inter-sensor offsets. To address these challenges, we propose Test-Time Selective Adaptation with Token Shift (TSAT), which derives spatial and temporal adaptation signals from unlabeled test sequences for online optimization. Specifically, we design a controllable token shift auxiliary task, which imposes explicit spatial correspondence between predefined token translations and resultant localization offsets, generating stable annotation-free spatial adaptation signals. Furthermore, we introduce a temporal backward prediction auxiliary task to exploit frame-wise temporal dependencies, effectively mitigating cumulative localization errors in continuous tracking. To suppress interference from unreliable tracking samples, we develop a reliability-aware update gating strategy to screen valid adaptation signals and stabilize online parameter updates. Experiments on CM-UOT demonstrate that TSAT achieves state-of-the-art performance against existing test-time adaptation methods, exhibiting superior robustness under frequent modality switching and severe spatial displacement. Experiments across tracking frameworks and datasets further validate the effectiveness and generalization capability of TSAT.

Abstract:Frozen vision-language models often match concepts mentioned in a caption without respecting their negation: a query "a kitchen with no toaster" favors an image containing a toaster. A lightweight text decomposer, NegSplit, identifies this structure by extracting negated spans and the remaining affirmative context. When no affirmative content remains, it queries the denied object's presence and reflects the evidence around a reference to score the negated description. 164. 【2611.15044】Estimating Image Creativity

Abstract:What makes an image creative? Although this may seem like a highly subjective decision, research in psychology suggests that creativity may be based on a set of fundamental creativity dimensions such as novelty, surprise, and arousal. A deeper understanding of image creativity can benefit both research and practical applications. Exploring how human viewers use creativity dimensions to evaluate image creativity may allow us to predict a target image's human-rated creativity automatically. We present a novel framework to estimate the perceived creativity of an image by: (1) predicting the strengths of an image's novelty, surprise, and arousal creativity dimensions, and (2) combining the creativity dimension strengths to estimate an image creativity score. Controlled human-subject experiments were conducted on Amazon Mechanical Turk to collect data to train supervised machine learning models to estimate an image's strengths on the three creativity dimensions. A final machine learning model takes the predicted dimension strengths as input to produce an estimated image creativity score. Results showed that our estimated creativity scores are statistically equivalent to human ratings of creativity for the images we tested. The novel contributions of our research are: (1) identification and validation of three psychological creativity dimensions used to estimate image creativity; (2) supervised machine learning models to automatically estimate novelty, surprise, and arousal strengths for an input image; (3) a supervised machine learning model to predict a creativity score from novelty, surprise, and arousal strengths for an input image, and (4) experimental methods to confirm the accuracy, advantages, and limitations of our approach.

166. 【2611.15039】Back to the Question: Tracing Visual Distraction Through Text Tokens

Abstract:The visual world is cluttered: robust vision-language reasoning requires ignoring irrelevant information. Yet vision-language models (VLMs) can suffer substantial accuracy losses when answering questions about a target image with distractors present. Through a systematic analysis of three open 7-8B VLMs on five perception benchmarks adapted to include distractor images, we show that distractors reduce accuracy even when models correctly identify the relevant image, suggesting that selection alone is not enough. Without directly constraining attention, this objective reduces middle-layer attention from question tokens to distractor images, consistent with the pathway our analysis implicates. With five distractors, our approach improves circular accuracy by an average of 16 percentage points over the Qwen2.5-VL baseline across the five benchmarks while preserving single-image performance.

Abstract:Backdoor attacks threaten the integrity of machine learning models by allowing attackers to control model behavior through triggers. Models can be compromised during finetuning by backdoor attacks through either poisoned data or adversarial training objectives. Because existing finetuning-activated attacks assume limited domain shift or frozen encoder layers, they often fail under full-model finetuning. We target a stealthy finetuning-activated attack where a dormant backdoor is implanted in a pretrained encoder, and later activated by finetuning on clean downstream data. We propose Poison-then-Hide, a novel attack that remains effective when the entire model is finetuned in a domain transfer. Our approach consists of three components: trigger optimization, base encoder poisoning, and targeted unlearning to conceal the backdoor. We evaluate our method on six datasets and three model architectures, and achieve state-of-the-art (up to 97%) attack success rates. We find that jointly learning the benign target task alongside the poisoning is critical to the attack's success. We demonstrate standard detection and mitigation defenses cannot fully remove the backdoor, which can reappear after benign finetuning.

Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway also encodes spatial information in a higher-rank, probe-decodable form, but is not the causal handle. To separate decodability from causal use, we analyze concentration, alignment, and semantic location. These diagnostics explain why behavior, probing, and intervention can diverge. Abstract:AI-manipulated video detectors are typically evaluated on clean, curated datasets. In deployment, however, videos have usually passed through repost compression on social-media platforms and sometimes were captured by imperfect hardware. To measure detection under these conditions, we introduce Reality Perception Gap (RPG), a benchmark of 10,000 videos from frontier generators and partially synthetic edits, processed with cross-platform repost compression and paired with real footage that carries camera-side optical artifacts. RPG also includes socially fragile content, such as crime and wartime footage, where fabricated videos can cause severe social harm. Across 18 detectors, none catches more than 15% of fakes at a 1% false-positive rate. A positive control and a re-encoding sweep separate two sources of failure: generator and content shift degrades detectors before any compression, and repost compression erases the low-level traces that the artifact-based detectors relies on. Existing detectors therefore struggle when deployment conditions strip away the generation artifacts they rely on. These complementary failures suggest that robust detection requires training under deployment conditions and combining low-level, temporal, and semantic evidence, where passive detection may have reached its limits.

Abstract:Assessing human creativity from drawings provides a scalable way to evaluate human creative ability. However, existing approaches either rely on costly expert annotation or treat creativity as a single regression target, overlooking its underlying structure. Motivated by this principle, we recast creativity as structured semantic deviation between paired drawings, where novelty measures the extent of departure from the original base sketch, and appropriateness determines whether such departures remain meaningful. This formulation naturally leads to a hyperbolic representation, in which novelty is quantified by geodesic distance and appropriateness is evaluated conditionally via a learned decision boundary, further regulated by an abstraction-conditioned adaptive constraint. Abstract:AI-generated content (AIGC) has substantially narrowed the visual gap between natural and synthetic images, while existing detectors often rely on generator-specific artifacts and exhibit limited generalization to unseen models. We integrate these physics-enriched descriptions with image representations via a native physics-guided multimodal framework, adapting CLIP ViT-L 14 with LoRA. At inference, the model requires only the input image, with no external captions or manual prompts. On GenImage, our method achieves 99.0 percent accuracy on SDv1.4 and 96.7 percent on Wukong, with a mean of 97.23 percent across eight generative models versus 95.8 percent for C2pCLIP under the same setting. Abstract:Inertial odometry (IO) using only Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enables camera-free head tracking in head-mounted devices such as VR headsets, AR glasses, and earbuds. Yaw augmentation improves robustness but does not guarantee equivariance; learned equivariant layers achieve it, but EqNIO's full pipeline costs nearly 3$\times$ the FLOPs of ours. While raw body-frame IMU inputs are inherently yaw-invariant, head tilt redistributes both gravity and motion signals across device axes, making the representation tilt-variant. We propose HeadIO, which combines a body-frame heading decomposition with a bidirectional Mamba backbone for head-mounted inertial odometry. Our decomposition achieves tilt invariance by separating gravity-aligned and horizontal components using only the tilt component of device orientation. We evaluate on four head-mounted datasets and find that HeadIO improves RTE-5s by 8.1% (0.260 m $\to$ 0.239 m) over world-frame methods with learned equivariant layers on Nymeria, the largest benchmark dataset, at nearly 3$\times$ lower FLOPs and 8$\times$ fewer parameters. Abstract:Cross-domain video deepfake detection increasingly uses frozen foundation-model experts, combined by calibrated score averaging, a per-video router picking one expert, or a learned head over concatenated features. Expressive routing and feature fusion are often reported to beat plain averaging. Across a 22-dataset frozen-expert testbed, we find those gains are largely evaluation artifacts. A corner theorem locates the gap routing aims to close: because AUC depends only on score ordering, the best any score-space router can do is an oracle reading the test label to pick each video's expert, a ceiling no realisable, label-blind router reaches. The theorem does not order real routers against a calibrated global average; the case against routing is empirical, and no router we test beats that average. Feature fusion reads raw features, falls outside the theorem, and is audited empirically. Reported gains trace to leakage: holding out one dataset leaks siblings sharing identities and reals (over-crediting routing), while holding out one manipulation keeps that dataset's reals in training (over-crediting feature fusion). A $2\times 2$ over fold and evaluation granularity pins the $+2.6$pp feature-fusion "win" to the fold alone: 12/12 significant under leaky folds vs. 0/12 under honest family-held-out folds, where both gains vanish. Fusion still pays off in the tail of hard videos and families: as experts are added, videos every expert misclassifies drop from 15.2% to 2.3%, and global calibrated fusion (InvB) beats the best single expert on worst-family AUC, selective risk (AURC), and low-false-positive recall, stably across protocols. Practitioners should calibrate and combine globally, hold out whole dataset families, and measure tail performance. For score-space routing under ranking metrics, honest evaluation and expert diversity matter more than combiner complexity.

Abstract:Open-weight Vision-Language Models (VLMs) score 85-94% on spatial benchmarks (BLINK Spatial, What's Up CLEVR) yet collapse to chance on simple geometric questions when object, scene, and texture priors are stripped away. Abstract:Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. Abstract:As particle-based simulations grow in scale, efficient compression of scientific data becomes critical. This key difference limits the effectiveness of the octree data structure that underpins most PCC methods. Neural codecs achieve only marginal bitrate reductions over the traditional G-PCC baseline on scientific data, revealing a significant performance gap. Supported by an evaluation spanning domains of cosmology, molecular dynamics, and plasma physics, we outline where the structure of scientific data limits current neural approaches and where learning can help in the future.

Abstract:Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the predicted future. The BEV, rendered from scene annotations for training, depicts roads and vehicles as simple shapes at a fixed metric scale, providing a top-down view of their positions and motion with reduced occlusion between vehicles. Perspective video, by contrast, retains scene details that the BEV omits, such as traffic signals and object appearance. Joint attention between two video diffusion transformers, one per stream, lets each stream inform the other during generation. The predicted BEV also provides a geometric interface for ego control: we translate and rotate its latest frame along an input ego trajectory and use the resulting frames as a soft condition that shows how the scene would appear to move if only the ego vehicle moved. At inference, BirdDreams generates both videos from a single camera image without requiring an HD map or vehicle-state inputs. On PhysicalAI-AV and nuScenes, BirdDreams follows input ego trajectories more faithfully than prior driving world models and generates more plausible ego motion without ego-action conditioning. Human evaluation shows that BirdDreams outperforms a perspective-only baseline in generating realistic surrounding-vehicle behavior.

Abstract:Multi-camera rigs ship pre-calibrated from the manufacturer, but their calibration goes stale each time the rig is repositioned, and drifts continuously through wear, thermal cycling, and vibration. Recovering it on-the-fly is hard: classical bundle adjustment needs a fresh multi-view capture and a global optimization whose cost grows with the rig, ruling out real-time use. In this paper we present RECALL, a feed-forward method that recalibrates a movable multi-camera rig in a single pass. From the nominal OEM calibration as an anchor and a brief observation of a known object, it predicts each camera's current intrinsics and extrinsics, written as a shared global rotation of the rig composed with a small per-camera drift. Instead of regressing the calibration in one shot, RECALL refines its estimate with a learned, rig-coupled recurrent operator that reprojects through a differentiable projection and applies attention across the cameras at each step, and solves for the shared rotational gauge in-network with a learned Gauss-Newton step rather than regressing it. Because the ground truth is synthesizable, we train entirely on data generated on-the-fly and need no captured dataset. On a synthetic 10-camera benchmark, RECALL is more accurate than per-camera and rig-coupled joint bundle adjustment ($0.26^\circ$ vs $0.47^\circ$ rotation, $5.4$ vs $8.9$ px focal) and runs about $10^5\times$ faster at about $0.12$ ms per rig. On real data (TotalCapture, CMU Panoptic) it matches or beats offline rig-coupled bundle adjustment on absolute and relative rotation while running four-to-five orders of magnitude faster, and on the Panoptic surround rig it also matches the strongest image-only foundation models (VGGT, VGGT-$\Omega$, $\pi^3$) on relative pose while staying metric and about $15\times$ more accurate in focal length. Abstract:Englacial layers in radio-echo-sounding radargrams (subsurface ice images) encode the climate and flow history of ice sheets and glaciers. We address two challenges: reconstructing complete layers from partial detections across radargram profiles and validating layer continuity across adjacent tile boundaries. We introduce a slope-aware greedy fragment-linking algorithm that reconstructs full-width layers using row-similarity gating and an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) slope predictor. Each reconstruction receives a content-based hash ID for stable cross-radargram identification. For quantitative evaluation, we generate SyntheIce, a synthetic dataset of 600 radargrams spanning multiple complexity levels and realistic noise conditions, including 150 wide radargrams divided into four adjacent tiles. All samples include exact ground-truth annotations. We evaluate the dataset using XCheck, a consistency-based validation framework, extending its original two-image setting to four consecutive tiles and enforcing continuity at every boundary. This demonstrates the dataset's utility for developing and evaluating real-world annotation algorithms. Our findings extend beyond ice science: when spatial features are fragmented but retain consistent local geometry, trajectory-based linking is more reliable than appearance-based matching. Evaluation against expert-labeled real radargrams demonstrates high precision, recall, F1-score, and mean IoU, supporting the method's transfer to real-world data.

Abstract:Vision-language models such as CLIP can classify images into categories they were never explicitly trained to recognize, but accuracy degrades when test images differ in style or source from their training data. A common remedy generates randomly cropped and flipped copies of each test image, called views, and combines their predictions. Since some views miss the object, methods must identify which views to trust. The dominant approach uses prediction entropy to measure confidence and retains the most certain views. Other methods use signals such as embedding typicality. Despite repeated refinements of these scoring functions, the information they rely on, the model's own response to each view, remains largely unexamined. We investigate this choice while holding other pipeline stages fixed. First, we show that view selection, rather than the gradient update, accounts for almost all accuracy gains. We then examine whether entropy identifies useful views when predictions are wrong, despite at least one view predicting the correct class. In these cases, entropy ranks correct views above incorrect ones no better than chance, recovering only about one-twentieth of the accuracy recovered by an oracle over the same views. This finding holds across two image encoders and under a control ruling out an obvious statistical artifact. An exact analysis explains this limitation: entropy measures confidence but not which class a view favors. We identify an unused signal already available in the augmentation pipeline: the fraction of the original image retained by each crop. Ranking views by this quantity improves accuracy on 14 of 15 benchmark datasets over entropy and on 11 of 15 over the strongest scoring function tested. A pre-method measurement also predicts which datasets benefit.

189. 【2611.14677】Fast Slice-Wise Deep Learning Motion Correction for Spinal Cord Functional MRI

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14677

作者：Thomas Dagonneau,Sandrine Bédard,Nontharat Tucksinapinunchai,Uten Yarach,Loïc Le Folgoc,Pietro Gori,Julien Cohen-Adad

类目：Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：MRI time series, functional MRI time, Spinal Cord Toolbox, Respiratory and bulk, functional MRI

备注： 4 pages, 3 figures

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Respiratory and bulk motion displace the spinal cord between the volumes of a functional MRI time series. Current methods such as the Spinal Cord Toolbox (SCT) take several minutes per time series, and general-purpose brain tools register whole volumes, whereas the cord moves mainly slice by slice. We propose a lightweight convolutional neural network that regresses the in-plane translation aligning each axial slice to a reference. Two models, trained without motion labels, correct large and then residual motion. On a 3T (120 scans) and a 7T (59 scans) dataset, the proposed method improves on SCT on every metric (tSNR +10 to +25%, DVARS -20 to -38%), leaves almost no slice displaced by more than one voxel (0.1%), performs on par with a slice-wise AFNI variant and better than slice-wise FSL FLIRT, and runs in about 10 s per scan, about 30 times faster than SCT. The code is available at this https URL and the method is available in SCT v7.4.

190. 【2611.14608】FreeDeshadow: Shadow Removal for User-Specified Objects With Multimodal Prompts

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14608

作者：Zhiliang Wu,Jihao Gu,Kun Li,Hanyu Xuan,Hehe Fan,Meng Wang,Weisi Lin

类目：Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：perform global shadow, shadow, shadow removal, global shadow removal, target shadow region

备注：

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Existing shadow removal methods either perform global shadow removal or rely on precise shadow masks to guide restoration. Such paradigms limit their ability to selectively remove the shadow cast by a user-specified object in practical applications. To this end, we introduce an object-aware controllable shadow removal task, which allows users to specify a target object through a simple prompt and removes only its cast shadow while preserving other content. However, object-shadow asymmetry makes it challenging to establish accurate correspondence between the specified object and its spatially separated cast shadow and to confine restoration to the target shadow region. To address these challenges, we propose FreeDeshadow, a unified controllable shadow removal framework that supports both visual and textual prompts. It consists of an object-aware generator and a shadow-aware local refiner. The former interprets the user prompt and produces a high-quality shadow-free proposal, while the latter establishes the correspondence between the object and its cast shadow and constrains the generated changes to the target shadow region. To support training and evaluation, we further construct PCSRD+, a large-scale dataset containing 154,571 quadruples at 1024$\times$1024 resolution and covering six types of user prompts. The visual prompts include a dot, a line, and an object mask, while the textual prompts describe the target object using attributes, spatial relations, or states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FreeDeshadow accurately removes the shadow of the target object under both visual and textual prompts while effectively preserving non-target regions. It also outperforms existing methods in shadow removal performance and controllability. Project Page: this https URL

191. 【2611.08631】BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08631

作者：Qiren Wang,Mingyu Guo,Zixuan Wang,Weisong Shi

类目：Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Robotics (cs.RO)

关键词：Camera-based driving models, Camera-based driving, build a dense, planning horizon, driving models build

备注：

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Camera-based driving models build a dense bird's-eye-view (BEV) grid and spend the same computation on every cell of it, although the vehicle crosses only a few of those cells within the planning horizon. We present BEVCast, a two-stage BEV whose resolution adapts to the predicted driving path. A coarse pass encodes the whole scene on a grid of 4.096 m cells. A heat head trained on the recorded path assigns a heat to every coarse cell and the cells with the highest heat are refined into 1.024 m cells under a fixed budget. The remaining cells keep their coarse resolution, so the trajectory head reads a mixed-resolution BEV that still covers the entire scene and needs neither an HD map nor a navigation command. Against a full grid of 1.024 m cells with the same architecture and training recipe, BEVCast at a 10% refinement budget encodes 28% of the BEV queries and needs 66% of the BEV encoder time at batch size 1. On nuScenes its mean displacement error is 1.078 m against 1.149 m and its drivable area violation rate is 1.46% against 2.29%. On NAVSIM navtest its mean displacement error is 0.577 m against 0.598 m and its extended predictive driver model score is 82.51 against 81.28. Next to published planners BEVCast reaches a comparable error on both benchmarks without a navigation command. The resolution of a driving BEV can therefore follow the task instead of the grid.

192. 【2606.21115】MS-rPPG: Multi-spectral State Space Model for Remote Photoplethysmography in Driver Monitoring Systems

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21115

作者：Jiho Choi,Sang Jun Lee

类目：Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG); Image and Video Processing (eess.IV)

关键词：measuring physiological signals, cardiac activity, camera-based technique, technique for measuring, measuring physiological

备注：

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is a camera-based technique for measuring physiological signals, particularly cardiac activity. From the remotely measured signals, heart rate can be estimated, which is crucial for health monitoring. In this study, we investigate a driver health monitoring system based on remote heart rate estimation. However, driving environments represent uncontrolled settings where videos are subject to varying illumination conditions and frequent head movements. We introduce MS-rPPG, a multi-spectral framework that combines RGB with near-infrared (NIR) face video to alleviate rPPG estimation under challenging driving conditions. To combine the complementary features from two spectral videos, we propose a cross-spectral linear modulation (CSLM) strategy based on frequency-domain analysis. Moreover, we introduce MS-Mamba, a novel state space model designed to effectively model long-range temporal dependencies while jointly capturing cross-channel interactions between multi-spectral features. We collected a real-world dataset called MS-Drive, which was recorded from 50 participants while driving the vehicle. The proposed method was evaluated on the MR-NIRP Car dataset and MS-Drive datasets. The experimental results indicate that MS-rPPG shows better robustness and heart rate estimation accuracy than previous methods, highlighting its promise for driver health monitoring. The codes are available at this http URL.

193. 【2611.17111】Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17111

作者：Zhuangzhuang Ma,Rukuan Chai,Qianqian Ma,Yanghua Wang,Branko Bijeljic,Martin J. Blunt

类目：Fluid Dynamics (physics.flu-dyn); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：underground hydrogen storage, geological carbon storage, affecting geological carbon, groundwater contaminant transport, carbon storage

备注： 48 pages, 9 figures, 18 tables, including Supplementary Information

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Pore-space evolution and fluid displacement influence how rocks transmit and store fluids, affecting geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport. A single time-resolved micro-CT experiment may produce tens to hundreds of three-dimensional images, and segmentation is required to quantify physical properties and run image-based simulations. Traditional methods such as thresholding perform poorly on noisy, low-contrast images and need manual adjustment per image; 3D deep learning networks segment each image without temporal information, so their errors vary between images and could be mistaken for physical change. Here we introduce a transformer-based 4D segmentation framework combining spatial and temporal information. It uses sequential images to resolve ambiguous phase assignments and separate physical change from segmentation error. The method is tested on images of mineral dissolution: it measures pore-volume growth and rock boundaries more accurately than an equivalent 3D model that ignores temporal information. It also captures the increase in permeability verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations. The advantage transfers to another dissolution sample without retraining. On two other datasets of fluid displacement, it reduces spurious changes in predicted rock and porosity fluctuations and accurately identifies filling events. Spatiotemporal segmentation turns sequences of hundreds of three-dimensional images into more reliable quantitative measurements of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement without per-image parameter adjustment to support the analysis of time-resolved CT imaging.

194. 【2611.15758】Physics-based simulation unlocks scaling laws for generalizable MRI reconstruction

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15758

作者：Hong Shang,Zijian Zhan,Sen Jia,Xiang Fan,Jintao Meng,Yang Zhou,Xiang Zhou,Tianyu He,Xinran Chen,Qiaoling Zeng,Keyan Yu,Jianhua Yao,Dong Liang

类目：Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：holds great promise, translation remains bottlenecked, clinical translation remains, magnetic resonance imaging, reconstruction holds great

备注：

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Deep-learning-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction holds great promise for accelerating acquisitions, yet its clinical translation remains bottlenecked by poor generalizability across unseen scanners, populations, anatomies, and protocols. Gathering sufficiently diverse clinical datasets to overcome this bottleneck is hindered by high acquisition costs, privacy restrictions, and institutional biases. Here, we introduce Scalable Inverse Model (SIM), a framework that systematically co-designs physics-simulated training data, model architecture, and learning paradigms around scalability--leveraging compute scaling to overcome historical data bottlenecks and achieve robust zero-shot MRI reconstruction. Across 14 public and in-house datasets--spanning seven international centers, five vendors, field strengths of 0.3-7 T, over ten anatomical regions, more than ten acquisition protocols, downstream quantitative and molecular tasks, and a 150-scan blinded radiologist study--SIM demonstrates robust zero-shot generalizability, recovering fine anatomical details while suppressing aliasing artifacts where conventional deep-learning methods fail. Attention-map analyses confirm that SIM learns physically explainable, dynamically adaptive reconstruction primitives rather than anatomy-specific priors. SIM establishes a scalable, privacy-preserving, and democratized infrastructure for universal MRI reconstruction, providing a blueprint for generalizable AI across inverse problems in medical imaging.

195. 【2611.15370】Supervision-Aware Evaluation of MedGemma for Reference-Assisted Radiotherapy Contour Ranking

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15370

作者：Jaden Moon,Caiwen Jiang,Songlin Zhao,Wei Liu

类目：Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)

关键词：Radiotherapy contour ranking, support quality assurance, Radiotherapy contour, score construction, quality assurance

备注： 5 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Radiotherapy contour ranking can support quality assurance, but vision-language model (VLM) gains may reflect supervision, score construction, available inputs, or representation access. We evaluated frozen MedGemma 1.5 in a single-institution study, a 12-patient held-out HaN-Seg test, five-fold cross-fitting on 30 non-test HaN-Seg patients, and transfer without refitting to 120 SegRap2023 patients. On held-out HaN-Seg, a supervised readout of the final prompt state exceeded a supervised readout of the model's yes/no output probabilities by +0.3047 pooled average precision (AP; 95% patient-bootstrap interval [+0.2822, +0.3269]); the advantage persisted against a parameter-count-matched nonlinear control. A readout of projected visual tokens exceeded the final-state readout in cross-fitting and transfer (+0.0706 AP averaged equally across patients on SegRap; 95% interval [+0.0607, +0.0804]), while a structured panel-feature readout remained competitive with visual tokens. The anatomy-conditioned readout did not demonstrate an advantage over the native-feature comparator. These results motivate visual-token and structured-feature controls in medical-imaging VLM evaluations; outcomes were computational or synthetic, not clinical acceptability.

196. 【2611.14979】Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14979

作者：Jiayun Wang,Ram Daftari,Weijie Gan,Valentin Duruisseaux,Ruibo Wang,Armeet Singh Jatyani,Boris Bonev,Anima Anandkumar

类目：Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：GPU memory, ignores through-plane, MRI reconstruction, limited in practice, memory and compute

备注： NeurIPS 2026

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

197. 【2611.14975】Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14975

作者：Shreya Ajay Kale,Angad Ripudaman Singh Bajwa

类目：Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Computation and Language (cs.CL); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV); Machine Learning (cs.LG)

关键词：hide complete failure, Medical vision-language models, open medical VLMs, single diagnosis, hide complete

备注： Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Medical Reasoning with Vision Language Foundation Models (Med-Reasoner). 16 pages including NeurIPS checklist, 1 figure, 5 tables

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

198. 【2611.14947】One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction

链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14947

作者：Yimeng He,Yibin Xie,Yi Zheng,Yifan Gao,Lixia Wang,Yin-Chen Hsu,Yufeng Wang,Meng Lu,Debiao Li,Xiuzhen Huang

类目：Image and Video Processing (eess.IV); Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

关键词：Deep-learning unrolled networks, Deep-learning unrolled, unrolled networks, leading approach, approach to accelerated

备注： 10 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Code: [this https URL](https://github.com/hym97/LoopMR)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Deep-learning unrolled networks are the leading approach to accelerated MRI reconstruction. State-of-the-art models such as PromptMR+ learn a distinct block for every cascade, so their size grows with the number of cascades. Sharing one block across iterations avoids adding parameters, but earlier shared-weight models typically used a tiny block and produced worse images than models with distinct weights. Therefore, it remained unclear whether weight sharing itself or the choice of block was the problem. Recent advances in looped transformers, which reuse the same block across layers, show that they can match or outperform their distinct-weight counterparts on several tasks. Motivated by this, we propose LoopMR, which reuses a single Restormer block at every iteration as its core. Besides the current image estimate, the block receives data-consistency inputs and latent images. On four datasets covering the brain (CC359), knee (fastMRI), heart (CMRxRecon2023) and carotid (in-house), LoopMR significantly outperforms E2E-VarNet, PromptMR and PromptMR+ in PSNR and SSIM at every acceleration factor (p 0.01), with about 1/9 of PromptMR+'s parameters (10.3M versus 92.9M). It also keeps its lead at unseen acceleration factors and on an unseen dataset. With our transformer block, the shared model matches or outperforms its distinct-weight counterpart at 6, 12 and 24 iterations. At a fixed number of iterations, shared transformer blocks match or outperform their distinct-weight versions, while shared CNN blocks perform worse. These results suggest that looping one well-chosen block can outperform stacking distinct cascades in MRI reconstruction, with a fraction of the parameters.

1. 开源趋势洞察

  • AI智能体从“对话交互”迈向“技能封装”与“工作流原生化”。开源社区正在重塑AI的使用范式，大模型不再仅是聊天机器人，而是被封装为可插拔、可复用的“技能模块”。book-to-skill2将技术PDF直接转化为Claude Code技能，prompt-master14以零Token浪费实现精准提示词工程。结合微软推出的microsoft/agent-framework15与浏览器自动化扩展nanobrowser16，AI正深度嵌入开发、逆向工程rea12与内容生产hypit5的完整链路。洞察：2026年的AI竞争焦点已转向“Agent技能生态”与“多智能体协同编排”。提示词工程正在被标准化、可版本控制的Skill资产所取代，AI开发正从“写Prompt”进化为“装配工作流”。

  • 端侧大模型部署“傻瓜化”，消费级硬件成为AI算力新节点。随着推理引擎优化与量化技术的成熟，本地运行前沿模型已彻底跨越技术门槛。Strata13实现Qwen3.8-Flash-Next在普通PC上的一键部署，配合hermes-webui9与claudecodeui18等跨端UI层，打破了CLI工具的使用壁垒。洞察：云端API依赖正在结构性减弱。“Local-First AI”架构凭借数据隐私、零延迟与边际成本优势，正推动开发者工作站向“个人AI超算”演进，开源UI层成为连接底层推理引擎与大众用户的关键桥梁。

  • Rust语言垄断高性能基建，开启“传统重型软件”开源重构潮。本周榜单中Rust项目呈现爆发式渗透，从系统级清理czkawka3、前端构建rolldown19到数据管道dbt-core17，更出现了纯Rust零依赖重构Photoshop的photocraft11。洞察：Rust已跨越早期生态瓶颈，成为内存安全与极致性能的默认选择。开源社区正利用其零成本抽象能力，系统性重写过去被商业闭源垄断的重型生产力工具，软件基建的“Rust化”已进入深水区。

  • 开源价值回归“实用主义”与“证据驱动”的知识平权。登顶榜首的HowToLiveBetter1以破纪录的热度印证了社区对“反焦虑、重证据”结构化知识的渴求。结合免费域名基建DNSHE-FreeDomains6、安卓底层权限KernelSU8与安全研究库MalwareSourceCode10，开源精神正从纯代码协作延伸至生活指南与底层工具的“实用工具带”。洞察：在AI生成内容泛滥的当下，具备明确成本收益分析、原始出处溯源的“高信噪比”开源项目，正成为开发者与大众对抗信息噪声与不确定性的核心数字资产。

1. 开源趋势洞察

🤖 AI编程智能体迈入“多智协同与认知对齐”深水区
开源社区的关注点已从单点代码生成转向智能体集群调度与人类认知体验优化。superset13 与 agent-orchestrator18 的爆发印证了“百级Agent并行编排+全链路管控”已成为企业级AI研发的新基建；opencodex12 则通过通用代理网关打破模型厂商锁定，实现底层LLM的自由热插拔。更值得关注的是 i-have-adhd1 的现象级增长，标志着开发者开始反噬AI的“冗长废话”，开源重心正从“能力堆砌”转向“高信噪比、符合人类注意力机制”的交互设计。

🛠️ 开发者工具向“轻量聚合+AI/MCP原生”架构演进
碎片化的传统工具链正在被高度集成的新一代终端替代。dbx4 以仅20MB的Rust体积兼容90+数据库，并原生内置AI对话与MCP Server，清晰指向“终端工具AI化、协议标准化（MCP）、交付轻量化”的不可逆趋势。结合 lm-evaluation-harness17 的持续热度，AI能力的可观测、可评估与开箱即用已不再是锦上添花，而是基础开发软件的入场券。

🌐 数字主权意识觉醒，催生“去中心化媒体与自建网关”浪潮
面对平台算法茧房与订阅制壁垒，开发者正通过开源方案重夺数字控制权。SmartTube2 与 SimpMusic19 提供规则自定义的无广告影音体验；OpenWA15 实现通讯API的完全私有化部署；ipatool20 则打破应用商店的下载垄断。这股“自托管+反锁定”运动，正在重塑个人数字基础设施的边界，推动消费级软件向用户主权架构迁移。

洞察一：AI智能体迈入“自治执行”深水区，安全与监管成为伴生刚需
大模型已从“对话辅助”全面转向“自主决策与执行”。Pion3 试图让AI独立运营公司，而 ML研究智能体为何不过拟合13 则揭示了AI在科研探索中展现出的惊人泛化能力。然而，自治能力的跃升直接放大了系统风险与法律真空：OpenAI机器人知悉漏洞7 暴露了AI在供应链安全中的“双刃剑”属性；与此同时，前FTC主席呼吁严管AI17 与 Amazon诉Perplexity案19 表明，技术博弈已全面延伸至合规、版权与问责制。AI的工程重心正从“提升智商”转向“构建可控的自治边界”。

洞察二：底层系统性能优化迎来“反暴力计算”复兴
在算力成本与AI负载的双重挤压下，开发者正回归计算机科学的第一性原理，通过算法巧思与底层调优换取数量级的性能提升。eBPF CPU开销降90%5 明确标注“非AI生成”，依靠记忆化实现突破；自旋锁底层优化16、将标志位压缩至11位9 以及 Tokio高性能原则10 共同印证了一个趋势：当硬件红利放缓，极致的并发控制、内存布局与零拷贝架构成为破局关键。基础设施层（如 Cloudflare AKE优化TLS15）的精细化运营，正在替代粗放式堆硬件，成为工程团队的核心竞争力。

洞察三：交互范式重构与平台生态的“控制权”博弈
软件与硬件的边界正在被新的交互逻辑重塑。为Chat构建的图表4 标志着数据可视化正从“静态仪表盘”向“对话式动态分析”迁移，UI设计逻辑需全面适配LLM的流式输出。与此同时，平台依赖风险与硬件入口争夺战愈演愈烈：XCancel服务暂停6 警示了第三方生态对单一社交平台的脆弱性；而 iOS/macOS 27发布1 与 Steam Frame起售$105912 则显示，巨头正通过软硬一体的封闭体验与垂直场景硬件，重新划定用户注意力与开发者流量的护城河。

  • 智能体架构向“状态持久化与可验证执行”演进：当前Agent研究正突破单轮工具调用瓶颈，转向长程复杂任务的稳健交付。Apodex 1.19与Prime Agent14通过递归子智能体协同、持久计算与故障恢复机制，显著提升了长视野任务的连续性。结合AutoResearch4“生成-证据执行”双阶段设计，表明Agent正从“概率性输出”迈向“抗幻觉、可审计”的自主数字员工范式，工程与科研自动化（如AutoDev3、AgentScope 1.015）已进入可用临界点。

  • 多模态大模型重塑具身控制与空间感知边界：视觉语言模型正从“被动理解者”转变为“通用动作控制器”。Show-Harness12利用离散语义动作直接桥接VLM与机器人底层控制，实现跨平台零样本部署；OpenWAM20则通过模块化预训练提炼世界-动作模型的设计原则。同时，Marigold V213将Diffusion Transformer重构为单步流匹配深度估计器，印证了生成架构向密集预测与物理交互任务迁移的强劲趋势，视觉-语言-动作（VLA）的模态壁垒正在消融。

  • 端侧自适应服务与稀疏化打破算力垄断：大模型部署重心从“云端堆参”转向“端存算协同优化”。FreeToken8提出带宽自适应的MoE调度策略，动态映射异构本地硬件，使个人设备运行开源大模型成为现实。配合SAS18在Softmax内引入连续门控的端到端稀疏注意力机制，以及经典PagedAttention17的KV缓存管理思想，行业正通过算法-系统联合设计实现高吞吐与低延迟的普惠推理，边缘原生AI将成为下一代基础设施标配。

  • 音频基座模型攻克长程连贯与实时记忆瓶颈：语音与音乐生成正摆脱短片段拼接局限，向具备上下文感知与情感连续性的交互模型演进。AuK6统一了指令驱动的语音生成与编辑，YuE2实现了结构对齐的长音乐创作，而VoiceMem11创新的双脑流式记忆架构大幅提升了实时交互中的检索精度与情感个性化。音频模态正加速融入多模态Agent的实时交互闭环，推动人机对话向“类人陪伴”体验跃升。

TL;DR

Agent Demo 的核心可以只是一个 while 循环：模型观察上下文，决定是否调用工具，系统执行工具，再把结果交还给模型。但一旦进入真实产品，这个循环周围必须长出一整套 Harness。它负责管理入口、会话、规则、上下文、预算、权限、验证、观测和长期记忆，把模型的“下一步建议”变成安全、稳定、可恢复、可验证的系统行为。

这篇文章会沿着一次请求的完整生命周期，拆解 Agent Harness 的十个核心模块：Interface 让请求从 CLI、Gateway、ACP 等入口进入，Session 让任务在时间中保持连续，System Prompt 定义身份和规则边界，Context Manager 决定模型当前看见什么，Runtime 控制循环、预算和中断，Tool 让模型能改变外部世界，Skill 让 Agent 复用成熟方法，Orchestration 处理定时任务、长任务和多 Agent 协作，Hooks 与 Events 让系统可观测、可干预，Memory 与 Self-Evolution 则决定哪些经验值得留下。

真正区分 Agent Demo 和生产级 Agent 的，往往不是循环里用了哪个模型，而是循环之外有没有稳定的 Harness。模型决定下一步可能是什么，Harness 决定这个“可能”能不能落地成可靠的系统行为。

十大核心模块

有没有见过那种 Agent Demo？

一个终端窗口，一段 while True，模型说要调用工具，程序就执行工具；工具返回结果，再塞回模型；模型继续想，继续调用，直到它说“完成了”。第一次跑通的时候，确实很让人兴奋。你像是给模型装上了手和脚，它不再只是聊天，而是真的能读文件、改代码、跑测试、查资料。一个会行动的模型，好像就这么诞生了。

最小版本大概长这样：

这段代码没有错。事实上，很多复杂 Agent 系统的心脏，最后也还是这个循环：模型观察，模型决策，系统执行，环境反馈，再交给模型。但真正的问题通常不是“心脏会不会跳”，而是当这个小 Demo 被推进真实世界，它会很快撞上一堆不那么浪漫的细节。

用户关掉终端以后，任务还要不要继续？模型连续调用了几十次工具，什么时候应该停？一次测试输出几十万字符，难道全部塞回上下文？用户恢复三天前的会话时，项目文件要不要一起恢复？模型说“测试通过了”，它到底真的跑过测试，还是只是觉得自己应该这么说？再往后，危险命令需要审批，工具权限需要隔离，多个 Agent 不能互相覆盖代码，长期记忆可能会把错误经验记成真理，Skill 也可能越改越乱。甚至连“任务完成”这件事，也不能只听模型自己宣布。

到这个阶段，你构建的就不再是一个简单 Agent，而是一套围绕 Agent 运行的基础设施。

这套基础设施，我会称它为 Agent Harness。

你可以把它理解成 Agent 的操作系统。模型负责提出“下一步可能做什么”，Harness 负责决定它现在能看到什么、能做什么、在哪里做、做到什么程度必须停下，以及这次执行会不会影响未来。如果只看那个 while 循环，Agent 像一个聪明的实习生；如果加上 Harness，它才更像一个可以进生产环境的团队成员：有工位，有权限，有流程，有日志，有交接，有复盘，也有边界。

把一套 Agent Harness 拆开，大致可以看到十个核心模块：

  1. 交互与协议（Interface）
  2. 会话与工作区状态（Session）
  3. 系统提示词（System Prompt）
  4. 模型上下文管理（Model Context Management）
  5. 运行时与主循环（Agent Runtime）
  6. 工具系统（Tool）
  7. 技能系统（Skill）
  8. 任务与多 Agent 编排（Orchestration）
  9. 钩子、事件与可观测性（Hooks & Events）
  10. 记忆与自进化（Memory & Self-Evolution）

先用一张图把这十个模块放到同一个视野里：

flowchart TB    UI["客户端
Web / Mobile / Desktop / IDE / Terminal"]    IFACE["交互与协议适配
CLI / Gateway / ACP"]    LOOP["Agent Runtime / Agent Loop"]    CTX["模型上下文管理"]    ORCH["任务与多 Agent 编排"]    TOOL["工具系统"]    SKILL["技能系统"]    SESSION["Session 与 Workspace 状态"]    PROMPT["系统提示词构造"]    EVO["记忆与自进化"]    EVENT["Hooks / Event Bus"]    MODEL["Model Provider"]    ENV["执行环境
Local / Sandbox / Remote"]    UI --> IFACE    IFACE --> LOOP    LOOP --> PROMPT    PROMPT --> CTX    CTX --> MODEL    MODEL --> LOOP    LOOP --> ORCH    LOOP --> TOOL    LOOP --> SKILL    LOOP <--> SESSION    TOOL --> ENV    EVO --> PROMPT    EVO --> SKILL    EVO --> SESSION    EVENT -. 观测与干预 .-> LOOP    EVENT -. 观测与干预 .-> TOOL    EVENT -. 观测与干预 .-> SESSION    EVENT -. 观测与干预 .-> ORCH

这十个模块不是架构图上硬凑出来的十个盒子。

它们刚好对应了一次请求的完整旅程：请求从客户端进入，落到一个持续存在的状态里；系统为模型准备规则和上下文；Runtime 驱动模型与工具交互；复杂任务被拆分和编排；所有动作被事件系统记录；最后，真正有价值的经验被沉淀下来。

下面，我们就沿着一次请求的路径，把这十层拆开看。

模块一：交互与协议（Interface）

请求从哪里进入 Agent

故事从入口开始。

最早的 Agent 往往只运行在终端里。用户输入一句话，Agent 开始工作，模型输出什么就打印什么。CLI 同时扮演客户端、协议层和展示层，简单、直接、舒服。

直到同一个 Agent 要接入 Web、IDE、桌面端、移动端，甚至被其他系统通过 API 调用。

这时候你会发现，每种入口都不一样。

终端适合展示连续日志，却不适合展示复杂文件 Diff；IDE 能把修改定位到具体代码行，却未必适合承载几个小时的后台任务；移动端适合接收审批和完成通知，却不适合实时滚动几万行测试输出；Web 端适合多人协作，但它对断线重连、身份认证和权限隔离要求更高。

如果每个客户端都各写一套 Agent Loop，很快就会出现几个行为不同的 Agent。

CLI 支持恢复会话，Web 端不支持；IDE 用一套审批规则，桌面端又用另一套；同一个任务从编辑器切到终端，运行状态跟着丢了。用户以为自己在使用同一个 Agent，系统内部却像几条分叉的河。

所以，交互层最好尽早从 Runtime 中拆出来。

flowchart LR    CLI["CLI"]    WEB["Web"]    DESK["Desktop"]    IDE["IDE"]    MOBILE["Mobile"]    API["API"]    IF["Interface Layer"]    RT["Agent Runtime"]    CLI --> IF    WEB --> IF    DESK --> IF    IDE --> IF    MOBILE --> IF    API --> IF    IF --> RT

Interface Layer 做的事情，是把不同客户端的输入转成统一请求，再把 Runtime 产生的结构化事件翻译成各端能展示的形式。它可以表现为 CLI，也可以是面向前端的 Gateway，或者遵循 ACP 这类 Agent 通信协议的适配层。对 Runtime 来说，用户是在 VS Code 里输入，还是在手机上发起请求，并不重要。它只需要知道：请求属于哪个 Session，当前工作区在哪里，客户端具备哪些能力，用户拥有什么权限，以及这次请求能不能被中断、恢复或审批。

这里还有一个容易被低估的点：Agent 的输出不应该只是一串文字。

一个真实 Agent 在运行时会产生很多种东西：模型输出、工具调用、审批请求、文件变更、任务状态、产物链接、错误报告。把这些都揉成一段字符串，就像把医院的病历、处方、缴费单和检查报告全写进同一个聊天框里，能看，但很难用。

更稳妥的方式，是让 Runtime 输出结构化事件：

flowchart TB    Start["run.started"] --> Delta["assistant.delta"]    Delta --> ToolReq["tool.requested"]    ToolReq --> ToolRun["tool.started"]    ToolRun --> ToolOut["tool.output"]    ToolOut --> Decision{"还需要交互?"}    Decision -->|需要审批| Approval["approval.required"]    Decision -->|生成产物| Artifact["artifact.created"]    Decision -->|更新任务| Task["task.updated"]    Approval --> Delta    Artifact --> Done["run.completed / run.failed"]    Task --> Done    Decision -->|直接结束| Done

CLI 可以把它们显示成终端日志，IDE 可以把文件修改展示成 Diff，移动端只接收审批和完成通知，Web 端可以把长任务折叠成时间线。

这一层的关键功能包括：

  • 统一请求模型：创建会话、恢复会话、取消运行、提交审批、上传附件。
